drivingQuestion: Since rapist and seducer are derived from one another, why is only the rapist compelled to marry?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is completed and answered in ketubot.sugya106.

segments.he: אוֹנֵס שׁוֹתֶה בַּעֲצִיצוֹ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מִכְּדֵי מִיגְמָר גָּמְרִי מֵהֲדָדֵי,
segments.en: The mishna continues: «A rapist drinks from his vessel,» and the seducer is not obligated to marry the woman he seduced. «Rava from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi: Since» the halakhot of a rapist and a seducer «are derived from each other» with regard to the sum of the fine,

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא מפרזקיא לרב אשי
moves.summary: Rapist and seducer are learned from each other; the difficulty continues in the next unit
moves.about: since rapist and seducer are derived from each other, the seducer too should be compelled to marry

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא מפרזקיא לרב אשי: מכדי מיגמר גמרי מהדדי
edges.about: since rapist and seducer are derived from each other, the seducer too should be compelled to marry

unresolved.issue: the unit breaks mid-difficulty; its completion and Rav Ashi's answer are in the next sugya
